modifications: Design consultation only; no Godot or TiXL code is copied or translated.

From Godot FastNoiseLite: adopted the domain-warp composition (two decorrelated low-frequency lattice samples displace the base domain before octave accumulation) to break the grid alignment that magnification exposes. Rejected switching the base primitive to FastNoiseLite's Perlin or its gradient-warp variants: the existing tileable Perlin lattice is content-locked by published works, and bit-exact default output is a hard requirement.

From TiXL upstream PerlinNoise2d: adopted the Iterations/Gain spectral controls as octaves (1-8) and roughness (0-1), matching the upstream parameter semantics so authored TiXL references transfer directly.

Band limiting is project-owned: octaves whose lattice cells fall below two pixels fade out through a smoothstep on the base-frequency footprint (cells per pixel), opt-in via noise_filter so default output stays bit-exact.
Rejected Godot's cellular/worley noise types and fractal ping-pong gain: no authored work needs them and they would widen the shader contract without a consumer.
